title: Write the unit sbox8: the black box's keyed transform of 8-byte blocks
context: Write `bee_answer` in units/sbox8.c, in C, so that it answers exactly as the black box's function `sbox8` does (`reference/blackbox sbox8`): the same bytes for every input, or the same refusal. The black box is the only specification: find out what the function does from the binary, by running it and by reading its machine code. units/UNITS.md says what the unit is given, what it answers and what its file may hold; hive/charter.md says what counts as your own work (a reimplementation from the binary, never a copy of another program). The judge's cases for this unit are drawn by the black box itself (units/UNITS.md). The judge builds your unit several times and runs each build several times on cases it draws then: every answer must be the black box's, byte for byte. Your own check, inside the project's sandbox only (AGENTS.md says how): sh bee/check.sh sbox8.
